methods.name: verify_verifiable_credential
methods.doc: Verify a W3C-style credential transiently; no credential or claim is stored.

methods.name: get_issuer
methods.doc: Publicly query a provider's active verification key and revocation root so attestation submitters can construct proofs for the live root.

methods.name: submit_attestation
methods.doc: Validate a signed assertion and its proof before storing it. The persistent entry's TTL is extended on submission and during checks.

methods.name: configure_oracles
methods.doc: Configure the bonded oracle set. The admin supplies the token used for oracle bonds and the destination for slashed stake.

methods.name: register_oracle
methods.doc: Register an oracle after it authorizes depositing its bond.

methods.name: restake_oracle
methods.doc: Add more bond to an oracle whose stake has fallen below the minimum.

methods.name: remove_oracle
methods.doc: Remove an oracle and return its remaining bond. Admin-authenticated.

methods.name: set_oracle_threshold
methods.doc: Change the M in the configured M-of-N oracle quorum.

methods.name: submit_oracle_attestation
methods.doc: Submit individually signed KYC/AML votes. Returns true only when the M-of-N quorum is reached and the new record is committed.

methods.name: get_oracle_record
methods.doc: Get the latest KYC/AML result accepted by the configured oracle quorum.

methods.name: get_oracle_config
methods.doc: Public oracle configuration and registered provider count.

methods.name: register_hook
methods.doc: Register a rule-module hook contract. Admin-authenticated.

methods.name: unregister_hook
methods.doc: Unregister a previously-registered hook contract. Admin-authenticated.

methods.name: is_allowed_with_hooks
methods.doc: `is_allowed` plus every registered hook's `check(address)`. Returns `true` only if the built-in checks pass AND every hook returns `true`. Hooks are evaluated in registration order and evaluation short-circuits on the first failing hook (or the first failing built-in check), so a rejected address never pays for the cross-contract calls that follow it.

methods.name: set_aggregation_vk
methods.doc: Install the aggregation circuit's Groth16 verification key.

methods.name: set_zk_issuer_root
methods.doc: Authorize `issuer` for aggregated proofs with its credential-tree root (a BLS12-381 scalar, big-endian), or replace that root.

methods.name: update_zk_issuer_root
methods.doc: An authorized issuer rotates its own root, e.g. after revoking credentials; proofs against the old root stop verifying.

methods.name: verify_aggregated_kyc
methods.doc: Check an aggregated proof without recording anything.

methods.name: submit_aggregated_kyc
methods.doc: Verify an aggregated proof and record a `ZkAccreditation` for every subject. Anyone may submit: the proof is the authority. Returns the number of subjects accredited.

methods.name: zk_accreditation
methods.doc: Accreditation recorded for `subject` by an aggregated proof, if it is still unexpired.

methods.name: verify_holder_balance_range
methods.doc: Verifies that `holder` owns a balance exceeding `threshold` without revealing the actual balance.

methods.name: is_balance_threshold_verified
methods.doc: Checks if `holder` has an active, unexpired balance verification at or above `min_threshold`.

methods.name: configure_drip
methods.doc: Configure the router and cap-table ledger used by opted-in legacy claims. The cap-table must separately authorize this contract as a registrar.

methods.name: set_lockup
methods.doc: Issue #10 — set (or clear, with `unlock_ledger = 0`) the holding-period lockup for `holder`. Admin-authenticated. Used both to impose a regulatory-exemption holding period (e.g. a 12-month lockup) and, by setting `unlock_ledger` back to `0` or to an earlier ledger, to grant a partial/early release under a court order or approved exemption. Does not affect `mint` or `initialize`.

methods.name: get_lockup
methods.doc: The ledger sequence at/after which `holder` may transfer or burn. `0` means no lockup is in effect.

methods.name: clawback
methods.doc: Issue #12 — on-chain clawback engine. Deliberately implemented as a standalone path, NOT on top of `transfer`: a clawback is an admin-only, legally-authorized recovery mechanism (court order, lost-key recovery, regulatory enforcement) that must be able to succeed precisely when the holder cannot or will not cooperate — for example, their address has since been suspended in compliance, or they refuse to sign. Routing this through `transfer` would force it through `from.require_auth()` and the sender-compliance check, which are exactly the two things a clawback needs to bypass. It still validates the source balance (reusing `Error::InsufficientBalance`, since the failure mode is identical to a transfer's — see the PR description for why a new error code was not added here), and emits a dedicated `clawback` event so the recovery is fully auditable on-chain. Total supply is unchanged: recovered units are credited to the administrator so every unit of supply remains backed by an account balance.

methods.name: upgrade
methods.doc: Issue #11 — migrate this contract to a new WASM build without losing storage. Reuses `Error::Unauthorized` (3), already the admin-mismatch error for every other admin-gated call on this contract; no new error code is needed.
